names.mark_kimball_house_2108_prairie_coach_ho: 2108 and 2110 Prairie Avenue: the coach house the two houses shared on the alley

source.citation: Glessner House Museum, 'Rees coach house relocated', The Story of a House (blog), 1 October 2014, with a photograph of the coach house behind 2110 S. Prairie Avenue before the move.
what_it_does_not_supply: the north (Kimball) half, demolished in the 1930s
which face the photograph's three-bay front is, or where the carriage doors were
a date of building: 'may actually pre-date the Great Chicago Fire' is the post's belief
what_it_supplies: one building across the alley ends of 2108 and 2110, divided by a party wall in the middle from 1888
the south (Rees) half's size in 2014: 25 ft wide, 35 ft deep, 23 ft high
the full basement and the ramp the horses went down to it; carriages on the ground floor, the coachman upstairs
the flat roof behind level wall heads, and the segmental-headed upper windows, as the building stood in 2014
